claim_disclaimer: Selection of Z1 is NOT a claim that Z1 has an edge. It is the next candidate for preregistration and engineering only.

basis.terminology: Yahoo Finance generic/continuous futures series REFERENCING CME equity-index futures - NOT a contract-level CME feed

coverage_semantics_resolved.explanation: Yahoo's 730d label is a cap, not a literal lookback: the 1h response spans 875 calendar days. Those contain 724 New York dates across SIX weekday values, because the CME week opens Sunday 18:00 ET. Sunday evening bars belong to Monday's CME trade date, collapsing 724 NY dates into 618 CME trade dates. 626 weekdays exist in the span; 618 are present; the 8 absent are exactly US market holidays.

bar_time_causality.timestamp_semantics: bar OPEN; the bar closes at timestamp + 3600s
bar_time_causality.admission_rule: only hour-aligned timestamps (ts %% 3600 == 0) are loaded. This drops the trailing still-forming bar and the irregular early-close stubs - 25 such rows per market in the snapshot.
bar_time_causality.rule: every feature at hour t is computable only from bars closed at or before t; the primary outcome begins strictly after t closes

synchronization.rule: a Z1 observation exists only where ALL FOUR markets have a closed hourly bar at that timestamp. No forward fill, no backward fill, no interpolation, no fabricated zero return, no partial-market row.

roll_exclusion.basis: CME equity-index expiry = third Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec
roll_exclusion.published_convention: lead-month roll is the Thursday 8 days before expiry
roll_exclusion.frozen_rule: exclude every CME trade date in [expiry - 10d, expiry + 2d]
roll_exclusion.why_wider: the Yahoo generic switch date is UNKNOWN, so the window is deliberately wider than the published convention on both sides
roll_exclusion.cancellation_assumption: NOT assumed. Roll effects are NOT presumed to cancel merely because all four are US equity-index futures.
roll_exclusion.immutable: cannot change during development except for a demonstrated data-engineering error

gap_semantics.rationale: the CME day carries a 1-hour maintenance break (17:00-18:00 ET) belonging to neither session, so consecutive panel rows sit 2h apart once per trade date. That break is a normal feature of the instrument; a weekend or holiday gap is 47h+ and is excluded.
gap_semantics.sigma_window: the most recent 120 VALID returns at or before t. Gap returns are omitted from the window, never stitched. Requiring a contiguous block is unsatisfiable - a 120-hour window spans about a calendar week and therefore always contains a weekend - and the first implementation produced 0.00%% availability for exactly that reason.
gap_semantics.outcome_is_stricter: Y requires exactly consecutive hours and is CENSORED across the maintenance break, so it measures one homogeneous quantity rather than mixing in a higher-variance session-open gap once per day

cases.roll-excluded interval: the dates are removed from the sample entirely

gap_semantics.never: a multi-hour or multi-day price change is NEVER computed and labelled an hourly return; invalid gap returns are OMITTED from the volatility history, not fabricated

primary_outcome.sigma: std of the 120 most recent valid NQ hourly returns at or before t
primary_outcome.economic_justification: the hypothesised mechanism is transient price impact from an unconfirmed move. Such imbalances are resolved by index arbitrage and market making on a minutes-to-hours scale, so the next fully closed hour is where the effect should be STRONGEST. A longer horizon would dilute a transient effect.
primary_outcome.horizon_not_searched: chosen from the mechanism before any outcome; NOT selected by comparing 1h/2h/3h/4h results

secondary_horizons.status: DESCRIPTIVE ONLY, predeclared, no second Holm family, may never replace the primary

timeline: 3. all feature inputs for t become available (they use only bars closed <= t)
4. the prediction is considered formed at the close of bar t

censored_when.maintenance break: CENSORED - t+1 is not the genuine next hour
censored_when.roll exclusion: the observation is removed from the sample

primary_outcome.proof: mutating C(t+1) moves Y and leaves every feature at t bit-identical; proven in backtest/test_z1_causality.py section D

feature_family.normalization: z_m(t) = r_m(t)/sigma_m(t-1). The sigma window ends at t-1, STRICTLY before the return it scales, so a normalizer can never be contaminated by its own bar. Rolling only - no full-sample estimate.
feature_family.basket: z_B(t) = unweighted mean of z over {ES, YM, RTY}
feature_family.weights_not_searched: the basket is EQUALLY weighted by declaration. No ES/YM/RTY weight, lookback, lag or threshold is optimized against NQ outcomes.

features.name: divergence_1h
features.lookback: 120 valid hourly returns for each sigma
features.rationale: an NQ move the broad complex does not confirm is more likely transient idiosyncratic flow than broad repricing, so it should partly revert

features.name: divergence_session
features.equation: sum of (z_NQ - z_B) since the 18:00 ET session open through t, divided by sqrt(n hours)
features.rationale: session-scale positioning imbalance rather than a single-hour innovation
features.related_to: divergence_1h - same sign expectation at a different time scale. Declared as ONE family; Holm accounts for the correlation.

feature_family.no_variation_padding: three genuinely distinct constructs - an hourly innovation, a session-scale accumulation, and the common factor itself - not six variants of one variable

removed.name: basket_z
removed.status: diagnostic-only, never independently tested, never promotable

baseline.purpose: Z1 must add information BEYOND NQ's own state
variables: session_bucket = hours since the 18:00 ET open, categorical
prev_day_nq_return = NQ return over the prior COMPLETED CME trade date
baseline.test_form: the outcome is regressed on [baseline + one Z1 feature]; the p-value of the Z1 coefficient is the incremental test. A raw correlation already explained by NQ's own lagged state is NOT an effect.
baseline.z2_role: frozen baseline/control, never a competing hypothesis

prev_day_nq_return_definition.definition: OPEN-TO-CLOSE return of the IMMEDIATELY preceding eligible CME trade date
prev_day_nq_return_definition.formula: ln(close of that date's LAST panel bar / open of its FIRST panel bar)
prev_day_nq_return_definition.availability: that session closes 17:00 ET, before the current session opens 18:00 ET, so it is fully available at every hour of the current trade date
missing_when: the predecessor is absent from the panel
never: uses the current incomplete trade date
computes a multi-day return and calls it previous-day
walks backward until a convenient valid day appears
uses a Yahoo daily close unavailable at event time
prev_day_nq_return_definition.implementation_guarantee: the function contains NO loop, so it cannot walk backward

vix.reason: a daily VIX close is not available earlier the same trading day, so an intraday feature would need the prior completed daily value. That complication buys nothing for the primary question, so VIX is excluded rather than carried with a leakage risk.

B_internal_chronological_replication.rule: frozen before outcomes; never used to repair or retune the model

C_true_prospective_holdout.nature: DOES NOT YET EXIST at freeze time
C_true_prospective_holdout.accumulation_requirement: 126 ELIGIBLE CME trade dates. Calendar time after the freeze is NOT the requirement. A date counts only if all its bars are after the freeze instant, it is not roll-excluded (the September window may overlap the start of collection), and it is not partial (>= 20 of the 23 modal rows). Roll-excluded, missing and partial dates count for NOTHING.

partitions.terminology_note: data already existing at freeze time is HISTORICAL even where we choose not to inspect it. Only bars timestamped after the freeze instant are a true prospective holdout.

effective_sample.honest_statement: the effective sample is the TRADE-DATE CLUSTER COUNT, not 13,703 hourly bars. Hourly observations within a day are dependent and are never advertised as independent.

inference.primary: OLS with CR1 covariance clustered on CME trade date, Student-t(G-1)
inference.dependence_sensitivity: predeclared moving-block bootstrap over CME trade dates at block lengths 5, 10 and 20 days, 5000 resamples, seed 20260914

stage_2_replication.multiplicity: if more than one survivor enters Stage 2, Holm within the replication survivor family at alpha = 0.10
stage_2_replication.rationale: a raw same-sign coefficient is NOT confirmation: an arbitrarily tiny same-sign estimate would pass. A one-sided inferential criterion in the preregistered direction demands the replication estimate be distinguishable from zero in that direction. alpha = 0.10 is chosen because Stage 2 is a confirmatory follow-up on an already-screened hypothesis, where the cost of a false negative is higher than at Stage 1; it is frozen before outcomes and never tuned.

hierarchy_rules: a failed development hypothesis may NEVER be revived because it looks good in replication
no replication result may modify the development model
m is never reduced after seeing failures
a secondary relationship is never moved into the primary family
an untestable feature is reported NOT TESTABLE and never replaced

conditions: 2 effect sign matches the preregistered expected_sign
4 not concentrated in one period: dropping the highest-contribution decile of CME trade dates neither flips the sign nor reduces |beta| by more than 50%
5 internal chronological replication passes the Stage-2 inferential gate: same preregistered direction AND one-sided p <= 0.10 (Holm-corrected within the replication family if more than one survivor)
6 survives the predeclared block-bootstrap dependence sensitivity
7 remains incremental to the NQ-only + Z2 baseline
promotion_gate.on_failure: V3-Z1 closes NEGATIVE. No repair search, no threshold tweaking, no horizon switching, no mining the replication segment.

effect_floor.unit: standardized units: change in the sigma-normalized outcome per 1 development-SD of the predictor
effect_floor.justification: a PREDECLARED MINIMUM STANDARDIZED INFORMATION EFFECT. Below this the conditional association is too small to be worth carrying into a strategy phase at all, so the experiment would end there regardless of statistical significance. Frozen before outcomes and never tuned.
explicitly_not: evidence that any strategy would survive costs
effect_floor.scale_note: for orientation only: with NQ hourly sigma around 0.35% at an index level near 29,000, 0.03 sigma is roughly 3 index points = 12 NQ ticks = about $60 per contract at $20 per index point. This is an ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE orientation, not a cost model: there is no entry rule, threshold, stop, target, holding period or frequency model, so no expectancy follows.

prohibited_this_phase: any Z1 coefficient, correlation, p-value or hit rate

changes.what: removed basket_z from the confirmatory family
changes.why: ALGEBRAIC REDUNDANCY. The baseline contains nq_z = z_NQ(t). Conditional on it, span{nq_z, nq_z - z_B} = span{nq_z, z_B}, so Y = a + b1*nq_z + c*(nq_z - z_B) is the SAME model as a + (b1+c)*nq_z + (-c)*z_B. Measured on a synthetic design matrix: beta_basket = -beta_divergence to machine precision and the p-values agree to 14 decimals. They are one test written twice. Because the preregistered signs were NEGATIVE and POSITIVE respectively, the two expectations would have been confirmed or refuted SIMULTANEOUSLY AND AUTOMATICALLY, reading as independent support that did not exist.
changes.status_now: diagnostic-only; a component of the divergence equation; never promotable

changes.what: m reduced 3 -> 2, Holm alpha unchanged at 0.05
changes.why: consequence of A1; the slot is deliberately NOT refilled

changes.erroneous_claim: 0.03 sigma is about 3 index points, comparable to one tick plus commission
changes.correction: NQ outright tick size is 0.25 index points at $5 per tick ($20 per index point). 3 index points = 12 NQ ticks = $60 per contract. A realistic round trip of one tick of slippage plus commission is roughly $9-14, so 3 points is several times a round-trip cost, NOT comparable to one. The original statement was factually wrong and made the threshold look like a tight cost-based derivation when it was not.

changes.what: effect floor re-justified as an information effect
changes.why: a standardized beta is NOT trade expectancy. There is no entry rule, threshold, stop, target, holding implementation, frequency model or transaction-cost model yet, so no profitability claim can follow from it.

changes.what: replication gate strengthened from same-sign to an inferential criterion
prev_day_nq_return defined exactly and made non-bridging
prospective accumulation counts ELIGIBLE trade dates only

standardization.y_scaling: Y is already sigma-normalized by its own definition and receives NO additional scaling, centering or rescaling
standardization.estimated_from: DEVELOPMENT predictor values ONLY. No outcome is read. Replication and prospective values are never used to fit the scale.
standardization.missing_handling: missing predictor values are excluded from scale estimation and from the regression; a missing value or a missing scaler transforms to None, never to a substitute
standardization.degenerate_scale: zero or non-finite sd -> scaler is None -> feature NOT TESTABLE
standardization.frozen_for_later_stages: replication and prospective observations are transformed with the FROZEN development constants, unchanged
